chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Jamming with Lester Young in Chicago; moving into the Woodside with Harold West
summary: While in Chicago he and Harold West were Lester's jam rhythm section; in New York West put him up at the Woodside Hotel where Lester lived.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Before I joined Roy in New York as -- at the time my mother was ill, as I told you before, I would work around Chicago, and Basie's band would come through all the time. And Lester always liked to jam, and I was his -- Harold West and I was his official Chicago rhythm section. So we would just go all to the various -- go to all the various clubs and we would just play.
Is it true that all the major horn players carried their own rhythm sections for jam sessions?

No, they didn't carry them but they had their favorites. But in Chicago we would find Lester because -- and he loved to play with us. You know. We knew all the tunes and we had the beat that he liked, and so we would just jam all night long. All the different --- hang out and just play. And so when I went to New York, Harold left and went to New York before I did. And on the spur of the moment I decided to go to New York. I didn't have any money, and I saw Harold as soon as I got to New York, and he asked me what was I doing, I said, well I came into live and he said, well where are you staying. I said, well I don't have a place to stay, and I just got in town. He said, you got any money, I said around $7.00. He said, well come on up

to the Woodside and share my place. So I took my trunk, my bag and went up there, and Lester was living up there. And they --- Harold was a great cook, and we all would just stay there and wait for Harold to cook and Lester would wait for Harold to cook, and we just had -- it was like a little family there. And --
